mechanism.domainTask: repository-scale evolutionary optimization of SAT solver code
mechanism.populationDetail: Five seed solver repositories initialize the process, but later search is described as champion-challenger code evolution without a sufficiently specified persistent population topology.
mechanism.archiveDetail: A champion solver is retained as the incumbent and successful challengers replace it; the paper does not describe a separate ranked archive of multiple elites.
mechanism.replacementDetail: The paper combines a five-codebase initial portfolio with a later champion/challenger loop; it is unclear whether multiple solver candidates remain jointly eligible throughout later cycles.
mechanism.generationDetail: The Coding Agent makes broad repository-scale edits, but the paper does not establish the per-cycle parent repository or how the five initial solver codebases contribute to each offspring.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: The metrics driving reward change over time; PAR-2 is added after cycle 33, and verifier/evaluator/reward processing is manually authored.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: The survey's parent-selection section cites SATLUTION under Rank-Based Selection, but the paper does not give a complete per-cycle parent-sampling or lineage algorithm.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Repository-scale agentic evolution with co-evolving rule/compliance infrastructure and domain-specific formal correctness gates.

provenance.citationWarning: Current survey text cites SATLUTION under rank-based parent selection only. Paper evidence also supports prompt/coordination, role-based multi-model use, champion replacement, evaluation feedback, and staged/parallel evaluation. Population topology, prompt block details, and actual parent lineage remain underspecified; keep these qualifications visible.
